title: 台湾测试如何应对中国海上围攻
description: 储百亮, AMY CHANG CHIEN2026年7月27日北京某购物中心外的一块巨型屏幕播放的新闻画面显示，中国海警在台湾周边海域巡逻，摄于2025年。 Florence Lo/Reuters As armed Chinese ships expand patrols around Taiwan, officials in Taipei are more urgently testing how they would keep fuel and other vital supplies flowing if Beijing tried to choke off the island. 随着中国武装船只不断扩大在台湾周边的巡航范围，台北方面的官员正在加紧测试：如果北京试图封锁台湾，他们要如何确保燃料和其他关键物资持续供应。 China, which claims Taiwan as its territory, has in recent years rehearsed a blockade, using naval ships and military planes to practice sealing off access to Taiwan. 中国宣称台湾是其领土，近年来已多次演练对台封锁，通过海军舰艇和军机切断台湾的对外通道。 Taiwan relies on imports of fossil fuels for about 95 percent of its energy, and natural gas fuels half of its power generation. And the global shocks caused by the blocking of the Strait of Hormuz during the U.S.-Israeli war with Iran have highlighted the importance of securing energy supplies. 台湾约95%的能源依赖化石燃料进口，半数的发电量来自天然气。美以对伊朗战争期间霍尔木兹海峡受阻所引发的全球冲击凸显了保障能源供应的重要性。 Officials in Taiwan are exploring whether floating gas storage and processing terminals, emergency stockpiles, or even reviving nuclear power could help keep the island running in a crisis. 台湾官员正在探讨浮式天然气储存和处理终端、应急战略储备，乃至重启核能是否有助于帮助该岛在危机中维持运转。 They have held so-called tabletop, or wargaming, exercises to address a siege scenario, and are planning to conduct drills to escort and reroute ships to port and to store and distribute supplies on Taiwan, four officials said. They spoke on the condition of anonymity to discuss internal government deliberations. 四名官员表示，相关部门已就围困情境举行了所谓桌上兵棋推演，演练为船只护航、调整航线入港，以及在台湾岛内储存和分发物资。因涉及政府内部讨论，上述官员要求匿名。 Worries about the threats posed by China have sharpened since last month, when Beijing announced its coast guard ships would conduct “routine law-enforcement patrols” in the waters east of Taiwan. That expanse of ocean matters because it is where Taiwan would most likely look for the United States and its allies to bring military and economic relief if China attacked. 对中国威胁的忧虑在上月进一步加剧，当时北京宣布，中国海警船将在台湾东部海域开展“常态化执法巡逻”。这片海域至关重要，因为一旦中国发动攻击，台湾很可能会指望美国及其盟友通过这里提供军事和经济援助。 Preparing for an Energy Squeeze 为能源封锁做准备 Keeping power plants supplied during a Chinese blockade would be daunting. Taiwan maintains at least 11 days’ worth of natural gas reserves, and has the capacity to store enough for up to 20 days. 如果中国实施封锁，要确保发电厂持续获得燃料供应将是一项艰巨任务。台湾维持着至少11天的天然气储备，并具备足够20天用量的能力。 “We’ve constantly conducted exercises on these national security topics, figuring out how to handle different scenarios,” Chen Chung-hsien, a deputy director-general of Taiwan’s Energy Administration, said in an interview. “We certainly view matters using worst-case scenarios.” “我们一直都在对这些国安议题做演练，针对不同情境我们要怎么样处理，”台湾能源署副署长陈崇宪在接受采访时表示。“我们一定会用最坏的情况来看这个事情。” Taiwan is exploring acquiring ships for storing and processing natural gas off shore, to provide additional capacity and for emergencies, Mr. Chen said. 陈崇贤表示，台湾正在研究采购可在近海储存和处理天然气的船舶，以增加储存能力，并备应急之需。 Chen Kuan-ting, a lawmaker from Taiwan’s governing Democratic Progressive Party who focuses on national security issues, said such ships could give Taiwan “more flexibility for how natural gas is received and dispatched” if China tries to seal off the island and threaten its infrastructure. 台湾执政的民进党立法委员陈冠廷长期关注国家安全议题。他表示，如果中国试图封锁台湾并威胁基础设施，这类船舶可以让台湾“增加天然气接收与调度的弹性”。 台北一场关于中国在台湾周边举行军演的新闻发布会。 But finding safer gas reception sites remains a big challenge. 然而，寻找更安全的天然气接受地点仍是一大难题。 Taiwan’s three terminals for receiving and storing liquefied natural gas are on the island’s west, where they would be highly exposed to attack or harassment from China during a crisis. The east coast is forbiddingly mountainous, with relatively narrow roads and small ports with no infrastructure for taking delivery from hulking natural gas tankers, or generating and distributing power from the gas. 台湾三座液化天然气接收和储存终端均位于岛屿西岸，一旦危机爆发，极易遭受中国的攻击或骚扰。东岸山势险峻，道路相对狭窄，港口规模较小，既无法停靠巨型天然气运输船，也缺乏利用天然气发电和输电所需的相关基础设施。 “The eastern region wouldn’t necessarily be the best solution,” said Mr. Chen, the energy official. “A floating pier on the west coast is more plausible, closer to existing power plants anyway.” “东部不见得是个很好的办法，”能源官员陈崇贤说。“如果是浮动码头在西岸的话比较有可能，反倒是比较方便你就近接近那些存在发电厂。” Taiwan’s government is also weighing whether to reverse its closure of nuclear power plants, which could be one source of stable power. 台湾政府也正在评估是否推翻此前关闭核电站的决定，因为核电可能成为稳定电力供应的来源之一。 Craig Singleton, the China program senior director at the Foundation for Defense of Democracies in Washington, said his group held a tabletop exercise about a Chinese “energy siege” of Taiwan last year with senior Taiwanese officials and company leaders. It was clear that “Taiwan urgently needed to diversify both its energy suppliers and the means by which those supplies reach the island before a crisis,” he said. 华盛顿智库保卫民主基金会中国项目高级主任克雷格·辛格尔顿表示，该机构去年曾与台湾高级官员及企业领袖共同举行了一次有关中国对台“能源封锁”的桌上推演。他说，推演结果清楚显示：“台湾迫切需要在危机爆发前，实现能源供应来源和运输方式的多元化。” China’s Threat to Taiwan’s East 中国对台湾东部的威胁 Even as they grapple with the threat of invasion, Taiwan’s officials are preparing for a murkier kind of coercion, in which Chinese government ships warn, restrict or even board cargo vessels approaching Taiwan. 在应对入侵威胁的同时，台湾官员如今也开始为另一种更加模糊的胁迫方式做准备——中国政府船只向驶近台湾的货船发出警告、实施限制，甚至登船检查。 The ships China has positioned on Taiwan’s east coast are part of what officials call “gray zone” tactics — hardball actions that fall short of outright warfare. Such muscle-flexing is hard for Taiwan to counter without risking retaliation from China. 中国部署在台湾东海岸的船只是官员们所称的“灰色地带”战术的一部分——即未达到全面战争程度的强硬行动。面对这种炫耀武力的行为，若台湾进行反制，稍有不慎便可能招致中国的报复。 Beijing has declared its jurisdiction over the waters in that area, a claim Taiwan rejects. In an early sign of how China could use its presence to assert its claims, a Chinese government ship stationed east of Taiwan radioed three passing cargo ships to request information, including about the crew members onboard. 北京宣称对这一海域拥有管辖权，但台湾对此予以否认。关于中国会如何利用它在该海域的存在来强化主权主张，一个早期信号已经出现：一艘部署在台湾东部海域的中国政府船只曾通过无线电联系三艘经过的货轮，要求它们提供包括船员信息在内的相关资料。 “What they did east of Taiwan was partly a very initial exercise to model a quarantine, meaning an operation to inspect and possibly turn back ships at sea,” said Lai I-chung, the president of the Prospect Foundation, a foreign policy institute in Taipei. 台北外交政策智库远景基金会执行长赖怡忠表示：“他们在台湾东部所做的，某种程度上是一次初步的隔离演练，也就是在海上对船只进行检查，并可能命令其掉头返航的行动。” China’s navy regularly places about seven or eight naval ships around Taiwan, including off the island’s east coast, according to Taiwanese security officials. 据台湾安全官员介绍，中国海军通常会在台湾周边部署约七八艘军舰，其中包括台湾以东海域。 “But now we’re also seeing more and more of the China Coast Guard,” Mr. Lai said, noting he was speaking in a personal capacity. The increased presence of the coast guard — a paramilitary force with large, heavily armed ships — would increase Beijing’s choices to put pressure on Taiwan. “但现在我们也看到越来越多的中国海警船，”赖怡忠说，并强调这是以个人身份发言。海警是装备大型重武装船只的准军事力量，它的存在规模不断扩大，将为北京向台湾施压提供更多选项。 5月，台湾总统赖清德在台北发表执政两周年谈话。 During a tabletop simulation late last month, President Lai Ching-te of Taiwan and his senior officials worked through a scenario in which Beijing demanded that cargo ships seek its approval before approaching Taiwan and sent coast guard ships to board, inspect and seize vessels. (In 2024, a Chinese coast guard patrol briefly boarded a Taiwanese ferry.) 在上月底举行的一次兵棋推演中，台湾总统赖清德及其高级官员演练了这样一个情景：北京要求所有驶往台湾的货轮必须事先获得中国批准，并派遣海警船实施登船检查，甚至扣押船只。（2024年，中国海警曾短暂登上一艘台湾渡轮进行检查。） Lii Wen, a Taiwanese national security official who described the exercise in a speech afterward, said that it “helped to pinpoint shortcomings in current response measures” and heightened attention on improving coordination between agencies on issues such as ensuring energy supplies. He declined a request for an interview. 台湾国家安全官员李问在随后介绍此次推演的讲话中表示，这场推演“有助于辨识现有应处措施不足之处”，并强化了各机构在确保能源供应等问题上加强协调的意识。他拒绝了本文的采访请求。 The Ministry of the Interior, which helped organize the June simulation, announced this year that it was planning disaster response drills on the east coast of Taiwan in September that would test receiving international medical teams and supplies. 协助组织今年6月推演的台湾内政部宣布，计划于今年9月在台湾东海岸举行防灾演练，测试接收国际医疗队和救援物资的能力。 Other exercises will most likely train officials from the ministries for the interior, economic affairs and agriculture to work together on distributing supplies within Taiwan. Escorting of ships approaching Taiwan would fall under its Navy and Coast Guard. 其他演练则可能侧重于训练内政部、经济部和农业部官员协调在全台分配物资。对驶近台湾船只的护航任务将由海军和海巡署承担。 China Is Ramping Up Tactics Short of War 中国正在升级低于战争门槛的战术 The Chinese coast guard ships currently off Taiwan’s east seem to be serving a mostly symbolic role for now. But that could change, Ryan D. Martinson, an associate professor at the U.S. Naval War College, said in emailed comments, also speaking in his personal capacity. 目前在台湾东部海域的中国海警船只似乎主要发挥象征性作用。但这种状况可能改变，美国海军战争学院副教授瑞安·马丁森透过电子邮件发表的评论中表示。他也指出这是以个人身份发言。 “Once the ships are out there on a consistent basis, Beijing is in a better position to take more forceful actions against Taiwan,” he wrote. “一旦这些船只持续出现在那里，北京就处于更有利的位置，可以对台湾采取更强硬的行动，”他写道。 The two coast guard ships China sent to Taiwan’s east this month weigh 3,000 and 4,000 metric tons, far larger than the coast guard boats Taiwan sent to shadow them. Ships from the Chinese Maritime Safety Administration, which regulates civilian shipping, also took part in recent actions in the same area. 本月中国派往台湾东部的两艘海警船排水量分别达到3000吨和4000吨，远远大于台湾派出进行伴航监视的海巡船。中国海事局——负责监管民用航运的政府机构——所属船只，近期也参与了该海域的相关行动。 Chinese government ships sailed near Taiwan’s main island 85 times during May and June, compared with 45 times in the same period last year, the Taiwan Coast Guard has estimated. 台湾海巡署估计，今年五六月间，中国政府船只在台湾本岛附近活动达85次，而去年同期仅为45次。 Coast guard ships come under Chinese military command and have been increasingly integrated in military exercises near Taiwan, said Julia Famularo, a lecturer at the University of Hawaii at Manoa who studies China’s maritime operations. 研究中国海上行动的夏威夷大学马诺阿分校讲师傅美珠(Julia Famularo)表示，海警船受中国军队指挥，并越来越多地参与在台湾附近的军事演习中。 The pressure from Beijing could increase before and after 2028, when Taiwan holds its next presidential election, said Taiwanese officials and experts. 台湾官员和专家表示，在2028年台湾举行下一次总统选举前后，来自北京的压力可能会增加。 “I think these gray zone measures will definitely become more and more intense,” said Jing Yuan-chou, an adjunct professor at Tamkang University in Taiwan, who studies China’s military strategy toward Taiwan. “我觉得那个灰色地带手段的强烈程度一定会越来越高，”研究中国对台军事战略的台湾淡江大学兼任教授荆元宙表示。 “For now, they prefer nibbling away at us, piece by piece,” Mr. Jing said. “But the nibbling lays the way for if they ever want to try to devour us.” 他说：“目前，他们偏好蚕食，一步一步蚕食，而蚕食是为万一要鲸吞做准备。” 储百亮(Chris Buckley)是《纽约时报》首席中国记者，自台北报道中国和台湾问题，重点关注政治、社会变革以及安全和军事问题。 Amy Chang Chien是《纽约时报》记者/研究员，常驻台北，报道台湾和中国新闻。 翻译：纽约时报中文网 点击查看本文英文版。

The east coast is forbiddingly mountainous, with relatively narrow roads and small ports with no infrastructure for taking delivery from hulking natural gas tankers, or generating and distributing power from the gas. 台湾三座液化天然气接收和储存 终端 均位于岛屿西岸，一旦危机爆发，极易遭受中国的攻击或骚扰。东岸山势险峻，道路相对狭窄，港口规模较小，既无法停靠巨型天然气运输船，也缺乏利用天然气发电和输电所需的相关基础设施。 “The eastern region wouldn’t necessarily be the best solution,” said Mr. Chen, the energy official. “A floating pier on the west coast is more plausible, closer to existing power plants anyway.” “东部不见得是个很好的办法，”能源官员陈崇贤说。“如果是浮动码头在西岸的话比较有可能，反倒是比较方便你就近接近那些存在发电厂。” Taiwan’s government is also weighing whether to reverse its closure of nuclear power plants, which could be one source of stable power. 台湾政府也正在评估是否 推翻此前关闭核电站的决定 ，因为核电可能成为稳定电力供应的来源之一。 Craig Singleton, the China program senior director at the Foundation for Defense of Democracies in Washington, said his group held a tabletop exercise about a Chinese “energy siege” of Taiwan last year with senior Taiwanese officials and company leaders. It was clear that “Taiwan urgently needed to diversify both its energy suppliers and the means by which those supplies reach the island before a crisis,” he said. 华盛顿智库保卫民主基金会中国项目高级主任克雷格·辛格尔顿表示，该机构去年曾与台湾高级官员及企业领袖共同举行了一次 有关中国对台“能源封锁”的桌上推演 。他说，推演结果清楚显示：“台湾迫切需要在危机爆发前，实现能源供应来源和运输方式的多元化。” China’s Threat to Taiwan’s East 中国对台湾东部的威胁 Even as they grapple with the threat of invasion, Taiwan’s officials are preparing for a murkier kind of coercion, in which Chinese government ships warn, restrict or even board cargo vessels approaching Taiwan. 在应对入侵威胁的同时，台湾官员如今也开始为另一种更加模糊的胁迫方式做准备——中国政府船只向驶近台湾的货船发出警告、实施限制，甚至登船检查。 The ships China has positioned on Taiwan’s east coast are part of what officials call “gray zone” tactics — hardball actions that fall short of outright warfare. Such muscle-flexing is hard for Taiwan to counter without risking retaliation from China. 中国部署在台湾东海岸的船只是官员们所称的“灰色地带”战术的一部分——即未达到全面战争程度的强硬行动。面对这种炫耀武力的行为，若台湾进行反制，稍有不慎便可能招致中国的报复。 Beijing has declared its jurisdiction over the waters in that area, a claim Taiwan rejects. In an early sign of how China could use its presence to assert its claims, a Chinese government ship stationed east of Taiwan radioed three passing cargo ships to request information, including about the crew members onboard. 北京宣称对这一海域拥有管辖权，但台湾对此予以否认。关于中国会如何利用它在该海域的存在来强化主权主张，一个早期信号已经出现：一艘部署在台湾东部海域的中国政府船只曾通过无线电联系三艘经过的货轮，要求它们提供包括船员信息在内的相关资料。 “What they did east of Taiwan was partly a very initial exercise to model a quarantine, meaning an operation to inspect and possibly turn back ships at sea,” said Lai I-chung , the president of the Prospect Foundation, a foreign policy institute in Taipei. 台北外交政策智库远景基金会执行长 赖怡忠 表示：“他们在台湾东部所做的，某种程度上是一次初步的隔离演练，也就是在海上对船只进行检查，并可能命令其掉头返航的行动。” China’s navy regularly places about seven or eight naval ships around Taiwan, including off the island’s east coast, according to Taiwanese security officials. 据台湾安全官员介绍，中国海军通常会在台湾周边部署约七八艘军舰，其中包括台湾以东海域。 “But now we’re also seeing more and more of the China Coast Guard,” Mr. Lai said, noting he was speaking in a personal capacity. The increased presence of the coast guard — a paramilitary force with large, heavily armed ships — would increase Beijing’s choices to put pressure on Taiwan. “但现在我们也看到越来越多的中国海警船，”赖怡忠说，并强调这是以个人身份发言。海警是 装备大型重武装船只的准军事力量 ，它的存在规模不断扩大，将为北京向台湾施压提供更多选项。 5月，台湾总统赖清德在台北发表执政两周年谈话。 During a tabletop simulation late last month, President Lai Ching-te of Taiwan and his senior officials worked through a scenario in which Beijing demanded that cargo ships seek its approval before approaching Taiwan and sent coast guard ships to board, inspect and seize vessels. (In 2024, a Chinese coast guard patrol briefly boarded a Taiwanese ferry .) 在上月底举行的一次兵棋推演中，台湾总统赖清德及其高级官员演练了这样一个情景：北京要求所有驶往台湾的货轮必须事先获得中国批准，并派遣海警船实施登船检查，甚至扣押船只。（2024年，中国海警曾短暂 登上一艘台湾渡轮 进行检查。） Lii Wen, a Taiwanese national security official who described the exercise in a speech afterward, said that it “helped to pinpoint shortcomings in current response measures” and heightened attention on improving coordination between agencies on issues such as ensuring energy supplies. He declined a request for an interview. 台湾国家安全官员李问在随后介绍此次推演的讲话中表示，这场推演“有助于辨识现有应处措施不足之处”，并强化了各机构在确保能源供应等问题上加强协调的意识。他拒绝了本文的采访请求。 The Ministry of the Interior, which helped organize the June simulation, announced this year that it was planning disaster response drills on the east coast of Taiwan in September that would test receiving international medical teams and supplies. 协助组织今年6月推演的台湾内政部 宣布 ，计划于今年9月在台湾东海岸举行防灾演练，测试接收国际医疗队和救援物资的能力。 Other exercises will most likely train officials from the ministries for the interior, economic affairs and agriculture to work together on distributing supplies within Taiwan. Escorting of ships approaching Taiwan would fall under its Navy and Coast Guard. 其他演练则可能侧重于训练内政部、经济部和农业部官员协调在全台分配物资。对驶近台湾船只的护航任务将由海军和海巡署承担。 China Is Ramping Up Tactics Short of War 中国正在升级低于战争门槛的战术 The Chinese coast guard ships currently off Taiwan’s east seem to be serving a mostly symbolic role for now. But that could change, Ryan D. Martinson , an associate professor at the U.S. Naval War College, said in emailed comments, also speaking in his personal capacity. 目前在台湾东部海域的中国海警船只似乎主要发挥象征性作用。但这种状况可能改变，美国海军战争学院副教授 瑞安·马丁森 透过电子邮件发表的评论中表示。他也指出这是以个人身份发言。 “Once the ships are out there on a consistent basis, Beijing is in a better position to take more forceful actions against Taiwan,” he wrote. “一旦这些船只持续出现在那里，北京就处于更有利的位置，可以对台湾采取更强硬的行动，”他写道。 The two coast guard ships China sent to Taiwan’s east this month weigh 3,000 and 4,000 metric tons , far larger than the coast guard boats Taiwan sent to shadow them. Ships from the Chinese Maritime Safety Administration, which regulates civilian shipping, also took part in recent actions in the same area. 本月中国派往台湾东部的两艘海警船排水量分别达到 3000吨 和 4000吨 ，远远大于台湾派出进行伴航监视的海巡船。中国海事局——负责监管民用航运的政府机构——所属船只，近期也参与了该海域的相关行动。 Chinese government ships sailed near Taiwan’s main island 85 times during May and June, compared with 45 times in the same period last year, the Taiwan Coast Guard has estimated. 台湾海巡署估计，今年五六月间，中国政府船只在台湾本岛附近活动达85次，而去年同期仅为45次。 Coast guard ships come under Chinese military command and have been increasingly integrated in military exercises near Taiwan, said Julia Famularo , a lecturer at the University of Hawaii at Manoa who studies China’s maritime operations. 研究中国海上行动的夏威夷大学马诺阿分校讲师 傅美珠(Julia Famularo) 表示，海警船受中国军队指挥，并越来越多地参与在台湾附近的军事演习中。 The pressure from Beijing could increase before and after 2028, when Taiwan holds its next presidential election, said Taiwanese officials and experts. 台湾官员和专家表示，在2028年台湾举行下一次总统选举前后，来自北京的压力可能会增加。 “I think these gray zone measures will definitely become more and more intense,” said Jing Yuan-chou , an adjunct professor at Tamkang University in Taiwan, who studies China’s military strategy toward Taiwan. “我觉得那个灰色地带手段的强烈程度一定会越来越高，”研究中国对台军事战略的台湾淡江大学兼任教授 荆元宙 表示。 “For now, they prefer nibbling away at us, piece by piece,” Mr. Jing said. “But the nibbling lays the way for if they ever want to try to devour us.” 他说：“目前，他们偏好蚕食，一步一步蚕食，而蚕食是为万一要鲸吞做准备。” 储百亮( Chris Buckley )是《纽约时报》首席中国记者，自台北报道中国和台湾问题，重点关注政治、社会变革以及安全和军事问题。 Amy Chang Chien 是《纽约时报》记者/研究员，常驻台北，报道台湾和中国新闻。 翻译：纽约时报中文网 点击查看本文英文版。

title: 北约一名加拿大华裔实习生因涉嫌从事间谍活动被捕
description: FRANCESCA REGALADO2026年7月27日位于比利时的北约军事总部，简称SHAPE。 Nic Edouard Bocquet/SHAPE, via Reuters The authorities in Belgium said on Saturday that a Canadian intern at the North Atlantic Treaty Organization’s military headquarters had been arrested on suspicion of spying for another country. 比利时当局周六表示，，一名在北大西洋公约组织军事总部实习的加拿大籍实习生因涉嫌为他国从事间谍活动而被捕。 The Belgian Federal Prosecutor’s Office said the woman was “of Chinese origin” and was arrested on Friday. “She is suspected of spying on behalf of a third country and of being a member of a criminal organization,” it said in a statement, which did not identify the country or the criminal organization. 比利时联邦检察官办公室表示，该名女子为“华裔”，于周五被捕。该办公室在声明中称：“她涉嫌代表第三国从事间谍活动，并涉嫌参与犯罪组织。”声明中未透露该国或该犯罪组织的具体名称。 The intern was first flagged by the security services at the Supreme Headquarters Allied Powers Europe, or SHAPE, which is near Mons, Belgium. The case was then referred to Belgian intelligence and a police investigation was launched, the federal prosecutor’s office said. 这名实习生最初被位于比利时蒙斯附近的欧洲盟军最高司令部(SHAPE)的安全部门发现可疑。联邦检察官办公室表示，此案随后被移交给比利时情报部门，警方随即展开调查。 That investigation led to searches of the woman’s home and place of work on Thursday, and a judge decided to place her under arrest on Friday, the prosecutor’s office said, adding in its statement that it would not comment further on the case. 检察官办公室称，调查过程中，警方于周四搜查了这名女子的住所和工作场所，法官决定于周五对其下达逮捕令，并在声明中补充说，不会对此案作进一步评论。 Canada’s Foreign Ministry and the Canadian Embassy in Brussels did not immediately respond to requests for comment on Saturday. 加拿大外交部及加拿大驻布鲁塞尔大使馆在周六没有立即回应置评请求。 SHAPE, which plans and executes NATO’s military operations, was cooperating with the Belgian authorities, said Col. Martin O’Donnell, a SHAPE spokesman. SHAPE负责规划和执行北约军事行动，其发言人马丁·奥唐奈上校表示，该机构正在与比利时当局合作。 “At this time, there is no indication that NATO or SHAPE operational readiness, command and control arrangements, or ongoing tasks have been adversely affected,” he said in a statement. 他在声明中表示：“目前，没有任何迹象表明北约或SHAPE的战备状态、指挥和控制安排，以及正在进行的任务受到了不利影响。” Lara Jakes对本文有报道贡献。 Francesca Regalado是《纽约时报》记者，报道突发新闻。 翻译：纽约时报中文网 点击查看本文英文版。

title: 特朗普全球新关税对中国影响有限
description: 艾莎2026年7月27日对华加征关税是特朗普为重塑全球贸易所做更广泛努力的一部分。 Qilai Shen for The New York Times China’s response to President Trump’s new round of tariffs was muted. Beijing issued a statement in protest, but unlike in past rounds of tit-for-tat, it did not lob a counter. 中国对特朗普总统新一轮关税的反应较为低调。北京发表了一份抗议声明，但与以往针锋相对的回合不同，此次没有采取反制措施。 China has cause to be low key. It has so far emerged from the trade war with the United States in a better position. One year ago President Trump threatened tariffs on Chinese goods as high as 145 percent. The levies that Mr. Trump imposed on Chinese goods on Friday were just 12.5 percent. 中国有理由保持低调。到目前为止，中国在与美国的贸易战中处于更有利的地位。一年前，特朗普总统曾威胁要对中国商品征收高达145%的关税。而上周五特朗普对中国商品征收的关税仅为12.5%。 Factoring in earlier tariffs, including those from Mr. Trump’s first presidency, the overall average weighted tariff on Chinese goods is now 23.1 percent. 考虑到早先的关税，包括特朗普首个任期内征收的关税，目前对中国商品的总体平均加权关税为23.1%。 Chinese officials are also confident that tariffs will not rise much further, after securing an assurance of a truce from U.S. trade negotiators. That agreement, which trade experts have placed at about a 20 percent cap, was later sealed with a handshake between China’s top leader, Xi Jinping, and Mr. Trump last October. 在获得了美国贸易谈判代表关于休战的保证后，中国官员也确信关税不会再大幅上涨。后来在去年10月，中国最高领导人习近平与特朗普握手正式敲定了一份协议。据贸易专家估算，该协议的关税上限约为20%。 The new tariffs will “have a limited impact on China at present,” according to analysts at Guojin Securities, a financial firm in Chengdu, China, who calculated the new overall tariff rate. The rate was previously 21.9 percent. 位于成都的金融机构国金证券的分析师计算了新的总体关税税率，他们表示，新关税“目前对中国的影响有限”。此前的税率为21.9%。 The tariffs imposed on China are part of Mr. Trump’s broader effort to transform global trade. On Friday, the administration issued tariffs on more than 80 trading partners over claims of failing to pass or enforce laws banning forced labor. The new tariffs, which were between 10 percent and 12.5 percent, replaced a global 10 percent tariff as it expired. 对中国征收的关税是特朗普重塑全球贸易这一更广泛举措的一部分。周五，美国政府声称超过80个贸易伙伴未能通过或执行禁止强迫劳动的法律，对这些伙伴征收了关税。这些新关税介于10%到12.5%之间，取代了随着到期而失效的10%的全球关税。 The White House issued the duties under Section 301 of the Trade Act of 1974, which allows the president to impose tariffs on foreign countries that engage in unreasonable or discriminatory trade practices. More tariffs are expected in the coming weeks, after an administration proposal to offset what the White House calls unfair practices in several countries’ manufacturing sectors — including China. This month, Mr. Trump also imposed a 25 percent tariff on certain products from Brazil that just took effect, and has threatened a 50 percent tariff on many Canadian goods starting in August. For both countries, the new tariffs could push their effective rates above China’s. 白宫根据《1974年贸易法》第301条款发布了这些关税，该条款允许总统对从事不合理或歧视性贸易做法的外国征收关税。美国政府提出了一项提案，旨在抵消白宫所称的包括中国在内的多个国家制造业领域的不公平做法，预计未来几周还会出台更多关税。本月，特朗普还对巴西的某些产品征收了刚刚生效的25%关税，并威胁从8月开始对许多加拿大商品征收50%的关税。对于这两个国家来说，新关税可能会使其有效税率超过中国的税率。 中国官方媒体周五将特朗普政府的政策称为“美国无休止的关税”，并称华盛顿“又找到了滥用关税的新借口”。 None of those tariffs are expected to top those announced by Mr. Trump under an international emergency law on April 2, 2025, which he termed “Liberation Day.” The Supreme Court struck down Mr. Trump’s use of the law to impose tariffs in February. 预计这些关税都不会超过特朗普于2025年4月2日根据一项国际紧急状态法宣布的关税规模，他将那一天称为“解放日”。 最高法院已于2月裁定特朗普援引该法征收关税的行为无效。 On Friday, Chinese state media called the Trump administration’s policy “America’s never-ending tariffs,” and added that Washington “has found a new pretext for abusing tariffs.” 上周五，中国官方媒体将特朗普政府的政策称为“美国永无止境的关税”，并补充说华盛顿“找到了滥用关税的新借口”。 The foreign ministry showed more restraint. Mr. Trump said Mr. Xi will visit Washington in September. 她还说，在下一轮关税中对中国征收任何超过7.5%的关税都会使脆弱的贸易休战面临风险，并招致报复。特朗普表示，习近平将于9月访问华盛顿。 Trade negotiators set that ceiling last year during U.S.-Chinese trade talks in Kuala Lumpur, the Malaysian capital. title: 中国再挥稀土大棒，将14家欧盟实体列入出口管控名单
description: KEITH BRADSHER2026年7月27日中国对德国最大的国防承包商莱茵金属公司征收了关税，这是中国针对欧洲对被指协助俄罗斯对乌战争的中国企业所采取的措施进行报复的一部分。 Georg Hochmuth/Agence France-Presse — Getty Images Last month, China blacklisted two American companies crucial to U.S. efforts to create a supply chain for making powerful rare earth magnets. 上月，中国将两家对美国建立强力稀土磁体供应链至关重要的美国公司列入黑名单。 On Friday, Beijing took similar action against even more companies in Europe. 周五，北京对欧洲更多公司采取了类似行动。 China’s Ministry of Commerce announced that it had banned any further shipment to 14 companies in the European Union of “dual-use” materials or products — items that China describes as potentially having both military and civilian applications. As a result, the companies may struggle to buy many of the critical minerals they need to make products like rare-earth magnets and semiconductors, which are essential for cars, offshore wind turbines, robots, drones and other advanced manufacturing applications. 中国商务部宣布，已禁止向14家欧盟公司进一步运送“两用”材料或产品——中国将这些物品描述为具有潜在的军事和民用双重用途。受此影响，这些公司可能难以采购制造稀土磁体和半导体等产品所需的许多关键矿物，而这些产品对于汽车、海上风力涡轮机、机器人、无人机和其他先进制造应用来说是必不可少的。 Over the past 16 months, China has used its dominance over the mining and processing of rare earths as leverage in economic disputes with trading partners. 在过去的16个月里，中国利用其在稀土开采和加工方面的主导地位作为与贸易伙伴在经济争端中的筹码。 In a statement on Friday, the Commerce Ministry noted that it had acted one day after the European Union imposed sanctions on 14 companies in mainland China and Hong Kong in connection with Russia’s war effort in Ukraine. The European Union said these companies, along with 24 Russian companies and 10 firms elsewhere, were “entities that are part of or support Russia’s military-industrial complex or enable the circumvention of E.U. sanctions.” 在周五的声明中，中国商务部指出，采取此项行动的前一日，欧盟刚刚对中国大陆和香港的14家公司实施了与俄罗斯在乌克兰战争相关的制裁。欧盟表示，这些公司连同24家俄罗斯公司和10家其他地区的企业都是“属于或支持俄罗斯军工复合体，或为规避欧盟制裁提供便利的实体”。 Many of the European companies targeted by China play a crucial role in turning rare-earth metals and other critical minerals, like antimony and tungsten, into alloys and specialty chemicals that manufacturers need. 许多被中国列入目标名单的欧洲公司在将稀土金属和锑、钨等关键矿物转化为制造商所需的合金和特种化学品方面发挥着至关重要的作用。 Also on China’s list was Germany’s largest defense contractor, Rheinmetall, which has been central to Germany’s effort to rearm after Russia’s full-scale invasion of Ukraine in 2022. Military hardware uses a lot of superhard tungsten and some rare earths. 中国的名单上还包括德国最大的国防承包商莱茵金属公司，2022年俄罗斯全面入侵乌克兰后，该公司对德国寻求重新武装的努力起到了核心作用。军事设备需使用大量的超硬钨和部分稀土。 Critical minerals have received growing attention in the West, especially since China imposed export restrictions in late 2024 on four critical but obscure minerals: tungsten, antimony, gallium and germanium. China then put export restrictions in April last year on seven kinds of rare-earth metals that are crucial to a very wide range of manufacturing, and has announced plans to impose restrictions in November on five more kinds of rare-earth metals. 关键矿产在西方受到的关注日益增加，尤其是自中国在2024年底对钨、锑、镓和锗这四种关键但鲜为人知的矿物实施出口限制以来。中国又在去年4月对广泛制造业至关重要的七种稀土金属实施了出口限制，并宣布计划在11月对另外五种稀土金属实施限制。 The Trump administration and the European Union are each trying to build mines for critical minerals and construct refineries that can turn ore into pure mineral powders and eventually into strong metal alloys. The production process is complex and can be dirty: Converting the powders into metals involves sometimes toxic chemicals. 特朗普政府和欧盟都在努力建设关键矿物矿山，并建造能够将矿石转化为纯矿物粉末、最终转化为坚固金属合金的精炼厂。生产过程很复杂，而且可能产生污染：将粉末转化为金属有时涉及有毒化学物质。 Almost all of the world’s capacity for rare-earth-metal conversion and alloy making is in China. Many of the European companies targeted by China on Friday are small and medium-size enterprises that hold what little expertise remains outside China for the advanced processing of critical minerals. 全球几乎所有的稀土金属转化和合金制造产能都在中国。周五被中国针对的许多欧洲公司都是中小型企业，它们掌握着中国以外仅存的关键矿物高级加工专业知识。 One of the companies on China’s list is Germany’s Sindlhauser Materials. Sindlhauser’s website says it makes yttrium alloys with zircon. Yttrium and samarium have been the two kinds of rare earths in shortest supply outside China after Beijing imposed export controls, with prices rising as much as a hundredfold. 德国的辛德豪瑟材料公司是被列在中国名单上的公司之一。该公司网站显示，它能制造含锆的钇合金。在北京实施出口管制后，钇和钐成为中国以外供应最短缺的两种稀土，价格最高曾上涨百倍。 Yttrium alloys with zircon are used in making advanced semiconductors. Makers of semiconductor manufacturing equipment have been complaining for months about acute shortages of yttrium compounds. 含锆的钇合金被用于制造先进半导体。几个月来，半导体制造设备的制造商一直在抱怨钇化合物的严重短缺。 Sindlhauser declined to comment on China’s action. 辛德豪瑟拒绝就中国的行动置评。 Another company restricted by China was one of Europe’s premier manufacturers of custom-designed electric motors with powerful rare-earth magnets inside, Italy’s Lafert Group. Lafert’s motors power many of the robots and other industrial automation in Europe’s factories. 另一家受中国限制的公司是欧洲首屈一指的定制电机制造商——意大利的拉法特集团，其产品内部装有强力稀土磁体。拉法特的电机为欧洲工厂中的许多机器人和其他工业自动化设备提供动力。 Beijing has been encouraging multinationals to move more of their supply chains into China, including buying electric motors from Chinese companies. While Beijing has severely restricted exports of rare earths and rare-earth magnets, it has allowed unrestricted exports of fully assembled electric motors with the rare-earth magnets already inside. 北京一直鼓励跨国公司将其更多供应链转移到中国，包括向中国公司购买电机。虽然北京严格限制了稀土和稀土磁体的出口，但却允许无限制地出口内部已装有稀土磁体的完整组装电机。 Rheinmetall and Lafert did not immediately respond to requests for comment. 莱茵金属和拉法特没有立即回应置评请求。 The European Union Chamber of Commerce in China has previously criticized the very broad dual-use designations on many critical minerals like those that China cited to restrict sales to the 14 European companies on Friday. 中国欧盟商会此前曾批评，许多关键矿产的“两用”认定范围过于宽泛，例如中国上周五援引的、用于限制向14家欧洲公司销售的那些矿产。 Keith Bradsher是《纽约时报》北京分社社长，此前曾任上海分社社长、香港分社社长、底特律分社社长，以及华盛顿记者。他在新冠疫情期间常驻中国进行报道。 翻译：纽约时报中文网 点击查看本文英文版。
content: KEITH BRADSHER 2026年7月27日 中国对德国最大的国防承包商莱茵金属公司征收了关税，这是中国针对欧洲对被指协助俄罗斯对乌战争的中国企业所采取的措施进行报复的一部分。 Georg Hochmuth/Agence France-Presse — Getty Images Last month, China blacklisted two American companies crucial to U.S. efforts to create a supply chain for making powerful rare earth magnets. 上月，中国将两家对美国建立强力稀土磁体供应链至关重要的美国公司 列入黑名单 。 On Friday, Beijing took similar action against even more companies in Europe. 周五，北京对欧洲更多公司采取了类似行动。 China’s Ministry of Commerce announced that it had banned any further shipment to 14 companies in the European Union of “dual-use” materials or products — items that China describes as potentially having both military and civilian applications. As a result, the companies may struggle to buy many of the critical minerals they need to make products like rare-earth magnets and semiconductors, which are essential for cars, offshore wind turbines, robots, drones and other advanced manufacturing applications. 中国商务部宣布，已禁止向14家欧盟公司进一步运送“两用”材料或产品——中国将这些物品描述为具有潜在的军事和民用双重用途。受此影响，这些公司可能难以采购制造稀土磁体和半导体等产品所需的许多关键矿物，而这些产品对于汽车、海上风力涡轮机、机器人、无人机和其他先进制造应用来说是必不可少的。 Over the past 16 months, China has used its dominance over the mining and processing of rare earths as leverage in economic disputes with trading partners. 在过去的16个月里，中国利用其在稀土开采和加工方面的主导地位作为与贸易伙伴在经济争端中的筹码。 In a statement on Friday, the Commerce Ministry noted that it had acted one day after the European Union imposed sanctions on 14 companies in mainland China and Hong Kong in connection with Russia’s war effort in Ukraine. The European Union said these companies, along with 24 Russian companies and 10 firms elsewhere, were “entities that are part of or support Russia’s military-industrial complex or enable the circumvention of E.U. sanctions.” 在周五的声明中，中国商务部指出，采取此项行动的前一日，欧盟刚刚对中国大陆和香港的14家公司实施了与俄罗斯在乌克兰战争相关的制裁。欧盟表示，这些公司连同24家俄罗斯公司和10家其他地区的企业都是“属于或支持俄罗斯军工复合体，或为规避欧盟制裁提供便利的实体”。 Many of the European companies targeted by China play a crucial role in turning rare-earth metals and other critical minerals, like antimony and tungsten, into alloys and specialty chemicals that manufacturers need. 许多被中国列入目标名单的欧洲公司在将稀土金属和锑、钨等关键矿物转化为制造商所需的合金和特种化学品方面发挥着至关重要的作用。 Also on China’s list was Germany’s largest defense contractor, Rheinmetall , which has been central to Germany’s effort to rearm after Russia’s full-scale invasion of Ukraine in 2022. Military hardware uses a lot of superhard tungsten and some rare earths. 中国的名单上还包括德国最大的国防承包商 莱茵金属公司 ，2022年俄罗斯全面入侵乌克兰后，该公司对德国寻求重新武装的努力起到了核心作用。军事设备需使用大量的超硬钨和部分稀土。 Critical minerals have received growing attention in the West, especially since China imposed export restrictions in late 2024 on four critical but obscure minerals : tungsten, antimony, gallium and germanium. China then put export restrictions in April last year on seven kinds of rare-earth metals that are crucial to a very wide range of manufacturing, and has announced plans to impose restrictions in November on five more kinds of rare-earth metals. 关键矿产在西方受到的关注日益增加，尤其是自中国在2024年底对钨、锑、镓和锗这 四种关键但鲜为人知的矿物 实施出口限制以来。中国又在去年4月对广泛制造业至关重要的七种稀土金属 实施了出口限制 ，并宣布计划在11月对另外五种稀土金属实施限制。 The Trump administration and the European Union are each trying to build mines for critical minerals and construct refineries that can turn ore into pure mineral powders and eventually into strong metal alloys. The production process is complex and can be dirty: Converting the powders into metals involves sometimes toxic chemicals. 特朗普政府和欧盟都在努力建设关键矿物矿山，并建造能够将矿石转化为纯矿物粉末、最终转化为坚固金属合金的精炼厂。生产过程很复杂，而且可能产生污染：将粉末转化为金属有时涉及有毒化学物质。 Almost all of the world’s capacity for rare-earth-metal conversion and alloy making is in China. Many of the European companies targeted by China on Friday are small and medium-size enterprises that hold what little expertise remains outside China for the advanced processing of critical minerals. 全球几乎所有的稀土金属转化和合金制造产能都在中国。周五被中国针对的许多欧洲公司都是中小型企业，它们掌握着中国以外仅存的关键矿物高级加工专业知识。 One of the companies on China’s list is Germany’s Sindlhauser Materials. Sindlhauser’s website says it makes yttrium alloys with zircon. Yttrium and samarium have been the two kinds of rare earths in shortest supply outside China after Beijing imposed export controls, with prices rising as much as a hundredfold. 德国的辛德豪瑟材料公司是被列在中国名单上的公司之一。该公司网站显示，它能制造含锆的钇合金。在北京实施出口管制后，钇和钐成为中国以外供应最短缺的两种稀土，价格最高曾上涨百倍。 Yttrium alloys with zircon are used in making advanced semiconductors. Makers of semiconductor manufacturing equipment have been complaining for months about acute shortages of yttrium compounds. 含锆的钇合金被用于制造先进半导体。几个月来，半导体制造设备的制造商一直在抱怨钇化合物的严重短缺。 Sindlhauser declined to comment on China’s action. 辛德豪瑟拒绝就中国的行动置评。 Another company restricted by China was one of Europe’s premier manufacturers of custom-designed electric motors with powerful rare-earth magnets inside, Italy’s Lafert Group. Lafert’s motors power many of the robots and other industrial automation in Europe’s factories. 另一家受中国限制的公司是欧洲首屈一指的定制电机制造商——意大利的拉法特集团，其产品内部装有强力稀土磁体。拉法特的电机为欧洲工厂中的许多机器人和其他工业自动化设备提供动力。 Beijing has been encouraging multinationals to move more of their supply chains into China, including buying electric motors from Chinese companies. While Beijing has severely restricted exports of rare earths and rare-earth magnets, it has allowed unrestricted exports of fully assembled electric motors with the rare-earth magnets already inside. 北京一直鼓励跨国公司将其更多供应链转移到中国，包括向中国公司购买电机。虽然北京严格限制了稀土和稀土磁体的出口，但却允许无限制地出口内部已装有稀土磁体的完整组装电机。 Rheinmetall and Lafert did not immediately respond to requests for comment. 莱茵金属和拉法特没有立即回应置评请求。 The European Union Chamber of Commerce in China has previously criticized the very broad dual-use designations on many critical minerals like those that China cited to restrict sales to the 14 European companies on Friday. 中国欧盟商会此前曾批评，许多关键矿产的“两用”认定范围过于宽泛，例如中国上周五援引的、用于限制向14家欧洲公司销售的那些矿产。 Keith Bradsher 是《纽约时报》北京分社社长，此前曾任上海分社社长、香港分社社长、底特律分社社长，以及华盛顿记者。他在新冠疫情期间常驻中国进行报道。 翻译：纽约时报中文网 点击查看本文英文版。

title: 安倍的“幽灵”：高市早苗捍卫“恩师”，推进民族主义议程
description: 赫海威2026年7月24日 Inside a hushed hall in Tokyo on a recent afternoon, Prime Minister Sanae Takaichi of Japan stood before a giant portrait of her mentor, Shinzo Abe, the slain Japanese leader, and bowed. 近日的一个下午，在东京一座安静的大厅里，日本首相高市早苗站在她的恩师、遇刺身亡的日本领导人安倍晋三的巨幅画像前，鞠躬致敬。 It had been four years since Mr. Abe, a giant in Japanese politics and the country’s longest-serving prime minister, was shot and killed while giving a speech outside a train station. Ms. Takaichi, his protégé, had come to pay her respects — and to vow to carry on his vision. She told the crowd of right-wing politicians, activists, journalists and business leaders that she sometimes still imagined him sitting on the couch of the prime minister’s office. 安倍晋三是日本政坛巨头，也是该国在任时间最长的首相。他在车站外发表演讲时遇刺身亡，至今已过去四年。作为他的门生，高市早苗前来致哀，誓言继承他的遗志。她告诉在场的右翼政治人士、活动人士、记者和商界领袖，她有时仍会想象他坐在首相办公室的沙发上。 “I could never fill Prime Minister Abe’s shoes; my days are filled with nothing but criticism when compared to him,” she said. “Even so, I want to be a fighter politician like him. I tell myself that I must be.” “我永远无法取代安倍首相；与他相比，我的每一天都充斥着批评，”她说。“即便如此，我也想成为像他一样不停奋战的政治家。我告诉自己，我必须做到。” 2014年，高市早苗（中）与安倍晋三在东京合影。 Since winning election nine months ago, Ms. Takaichi, Japan’s first female prime minister, has frequently leveraged her ties to Mr. Abe to rally support for her nationalist agenda, often referring to him and his policies in major speeches. 自九个月前赢得选举以来，日本首位女首相高市早苗频繁利用她与安倍的关系来为她的民族主义议程争取支持，并经常在重要演讲中提及他以及他的政策。 She has hailed his vision of a more muscular Japan that is a driving force for strength and stability across Asia. She has invoked his legacy to call for greater military spending and the establishment of Japan’s first intelligence agency since World War II. She has dropped his name while wooing foreign leaders such as President Trump and Prime Minister Narendra Modi of India. 她赞扬安倍晋三关于建立一个更强大的日本并使之成为整个亚洲力量与稳定驱动力的愿景。她援引他的政治遗产，呼吁增加军事开支，并建立日本自二战以来的首个情报机构。在争取特朗普总统和印度总理莫迪等外国领导人的支持时，她也曾提及他的名字。 Yet Mr. Abe remains a divisive figure in Japan because of his break with decades of postwar pacifism; his support for changing how the country’s World War II-era history is taught in schools; and a rise in economic inequality during his tenure. His killing, by a 41-year-old man who was protesting the ruling Liberal Democratic Party’s ties to the Unification Church, a fringe religious group, prompted a range of reactions. While many people were outraged, some sympathized with the assassin, noting his difficult childhood. Others said that a state funeral for Mr. Abe was a waste of money. (His assassin, Tetsuya Yamagami, was sentenced to life in prison earlier this year.) 然而，安倍晋三在日本仍是一个引发分歧的人物，因为他打破了数十年的战后和平主义；支持改变学校对二战时期历史的教学方式；在他的任期内，经济不平等现象出现加剧。他被一名41岁男子刺杀，该男子以此抗议执政的自民党与边缘宗教团体“统一教会”的关系。这一事件引发了一系列反应。虽然许多人感到愤怒，但也有人理解凶手，同情他艰难的童年。还有人说为安倍晋三举行国葬是浪费金钱。（今年早些时候，刺杀他的凶手山上彻也被判处终身监禁。） Despite Mr. Abe’s complicated legacy, Ms. Takaichi has emerged as one of his chief defenders, hailing him as a transformative leader who elevated Japan’s stature on the global stage. 尽管安倍晋三留下的政治遗产错综复杂，但高市早苗已成为他的主要捍卫者之一，她称赞安倍晋三是一位具有变革精神的领导人，提升了日本在全球舞台上的地位。 This triumphant account of Mr. Abe’s tenure has been on display recently across Japan, including at a sold-out exhibition by the Shinzo Abe Digital Museum, an organization founded by Mr. Abe’s allies in business and government. The exhibition featured more than 100 objects from his life, including the microphone he was holding when he was shot on July 8, 2022, in the ancient city of Nara, Ms. Takaichi’s hometown. 最近，对安倍任期的这种颂扬式叙述在日本各地展示，其中包括“安倍晋三数字博物馆“举办的一场门票售罄的展览，“安倍晋三数字博物馆“由安倍在商政两界的盟友创办。该展览的展品包括他生前的100多件物品，包括2022年7月8日他在古城奈良遇刺时手里拿着的麦克风，那里也是高市早苗的故乡。 安倍晋三的遗孀安倍昭惠（左）出席了一场展出安倍生前物品的展览。 Kentaro Takahashi for The New York Times2022年7月安倍晋三遭枪击时手中握着的麦克风。 Mr. Abe’s widow, Akie Abe, said during a visit to the exhibition in Nara on Sunday that her husband’s message “has been entrusted to” Ms. Takaichi. 安倍的遗孀安倍昭惠周日参观在奈良举行的展览时表示，她丈夫的使命“已托付给”高市早苗。 Same Playbook, New Challenges 相同的策略，全新的挑战 Ms. Takaichi, who met Mr. Abe in the 1990s when they were both rising politicians and later served in his cabinet, has sought to portray herself as the inheritor of his legacy, at a time when Japan is facing rising tensions with China, Russia and North Korea. 高市早苗在20世纪90年代结识安倍晋三，当时两人都是冉冉升起的政治新星，她后来还在安倍内阁中任职。在日本与中、俄、朝三国紧张局势不断升级之际，她一直试图将自己塑造成安倍晋三政治遗产的继承人。 “She’s embracing what Abe did and running with it,” said Sheila A. Smith, a senior fellow at the Council on Foreign Relations. “她正在全盘接受安倍晋三的一切，并以此为基础继续前进，”美国外交关系委员会高级研究员希拉·史密斯说。 The question now, analysts say, is whether Ms. Takaichi can adapt Mr. Abe’s vision to new challenges. Among them: 分析人士表示，现在的问题是，高市早苗能否将安倍晋三的愿景进行调整，以适应新的挑战。其中包括： • Beijing is rapidly expanding its military and economic influence in Asia, and has led a monthslong campaign against Ms. Takaichi to punish her for a comment she made in support of Taiwan, which China claims as its territory. • 北京正迅速扩大其在亚洲的军事和经济影响力，并针对高市早苗发起了一场持续数月的攻势，以惩罚她发表的支持台湾的言论。中国声称台湾是其领土。 • Japan’s economic outlook has grown more complicated as the country grapples with inflation for the first time in decades and a stubbornly weak yen. • 随着日本几十年来首次面临通货膨胀，加上日元持续疲软，该国的经济前景变得更加复杂。 • The country’s demographic decline is also accelerating, hurting the economy, causing labor shortages and undermining defense priorities like military recruitment. • 日本的人口衰退也在加速，这拖累了经济，导致了劳动力短缺，并削弱了征兵等国防优先事项。 Mieko Nakabayashi, a political science professor at Waseda University in Tokyo, said Ms. Takaichi was clinging to Mr. Abe’s playbook while ignoring new realities. She pointed to Ms. Takaichi’s support for expansionary fiscal policies, which some analysts say could exacerbate inflation. 东京早稻田大学政治学教授中林美惠子表示，高市早苗一味沿袭安倍晋三的策略，却忽视了新的现实。她指出，高市早苗支持扩张性财政政策，一些分析人士称这可能会加剧通货膨胀。 “Her popularity depends on Mr. Abe’s legacy,” Ms. Nakabayashi said. “Her biggest selling point is that she is trying to realize everything that Mr. Abe wanted to do, at whatever cost.” “她的支持率依赖于安倍的政治遗产，”中林美惠子说。“她最大的卖点在于，无论付出什么代价，她都致力于实现安倍想要做的一切。” 在日本与中俄朝紧张局势不断升级之际，高市早苗一直试图将自己塑造成安倍晋三政治遗产的继承人。 Ms. Takaichi worked for Mr. Abe during his first stint as prime minister in 2006, and during his second term, which began in 2012. She rose to the powerful position of minister for internal affairs and communications. 高市早苗曾在2006年安倍晋三首次担任首相期间以及始于2012年的第二个任期内为他工作。她一路晋升，升任总务大臣这一要职。 During that time she became a fierce defender of his policies, including efforts to revise Japan’s Constitution to unfetter its military, and his economic program, which emphasized cheap cash and government stimulus efforts. 在那期间，她成为安倍晋三政策的坚定捍卫者，包括旨在修改日本宪法以解除军队束缚的努力，以及强调低成本资金和政府刺激措施的经济计划。 “I was deeply drawn not only to his qualities as a politician but also to his character as a human being,” Ms. Takaichi said of her work with Mr. Abe, in a letter on display at the new exhibition. 在此次新展览中展出的一封信中，高市早苗如此描述她与安倍晋三共事的经历：“我不仅深深地被他作为政治人士的品质所吸引，也被他作为一个人的人格魅力所吸引。” Tobias Harris, the founder of the advisory firm Japan Foresight and the author of a book on Mr. Abe, said that it remained to be seen whether Ms. Takaichi had fully grasped the lessons of his tenure. He said it was notable that she identified with Mr. Abe’s fighting spirit, given that Mr. Abe’s success in his second term came in part from tempering those impulses. 咨询公司“日本远见”的创始人、一部有关安倍晋三书籍的作者托比亚斯·哈里斯表示，高市早苗是否充分吸取了安倍晋三任期内的教训目前还有待观察。他说，值得注意的是，她认同安倍晋三的战斗精神，而事实上，安倍晋三在第二任期的成功部分源于他克制了那些冲动。 “We have seen her willingness to bulldoze her opponents over and over again,” Mr. Harris said. “But as Abe learned, there is a cost to pay for that.” “我们一次又一次地看到她不惜碾压对手的意愿，”哈里斯说。“但正如安倍所意识到的那样，这种做法是要付出代价的。” 安倍晋三回顾展入口处的参观者。 The Shinzo Abe Digital Museum raised more than $338,000 from individual donors for the exhibition. On a recent day, visitors left notes on a wall with messages such as “You were our hope!” and “We will carry forward your mission.” A shop sold Abe-themed calendars and playing cards that included scenes of him golfing with President Trump. “安倍晋三数字博物馆”从个人捐助者那里筹集了超过33.8万美元用于此次展览。前不久的一天，参观者在墙上留下了诸如“您曾是我们的希望！”和“我们将继承您的使命”之类的留言。一家商店出售以安倍晋三为主题的日历和扑克牌，其中包括他与特朗普总统打高尔夫球的场景。 The exhibition became a gathering spot for his supporters, drawing nearly 7,000 visitors in Tokyo and Nara, including more than a half dozen of Ms. Takaichi’s cabinet officials. 展览成为安倍晋三支持者的聚集地，在东京和奈良吸引了近7000名参观者，包括超过六名高市内阁官员。 Mr. Abe’s supporters are hopeful about Ms. Takaichi, though they said she would face different challenges than Mr. Abe, including disruptions to the energy supply, foreign wars and political volatility in the United States. 安倍晋三的支持者对高市早苗抱有希望，尽管他们表示，她将面临与安倍晋三不同的挑战，包括能源供应中断、外国战争以及美国的政治动荡。 Fumiyo Kato, 48, who runs a weather data company in Tokyo, cried during a recent visit to the exhibition as she viewed Mr. Abe’s personal artifacts: a childhood notebook, a portrait of his father, a wedding photo. She said that Ms. Takaichi appeared to be carrying on his legacy, but it was too early to say whether she would succeed. 48岁的加藤文代（音）在东京经营一家气象数据公司。最近参观展览时，她看到安倍的个人物品——一本童年笔记本、一张他父亲的肖像、一张结婚照——不禁流下了眼泪。她说高市早苗似乎继承了他的遗志，但现在断言她是否会成功还为时过早。 “Abe was a great man,” she said. “He can’t be easily replaced.” “安倍是一位伟人，”她说。“他不能被轻易取代。” Hisako Ueno对本文有报道贡献。 赫海威(Javier C. Hernández)是《纽约时报》东京分社社长，领导时报对日本及周边地区的报道。在过去十年的大部分时间里，他一直在亚洲进行报道，此前曾任驻华记者。 翻译：纽约时报中文网 点击查看本文英文版。
content: 赫海威 2026年7月24日 Inside a hushed hall in Tokyo on a recent afternoon, Prime Minister Sanae Takaichi of Japan stood before a giant portrait of her mentor, Shinzo Abe, the slain Japanese leader, and bowed . 近日的一个下午，在东京一座安静的大厅里，日本首相高市早苗站在她的恩师、遇刺身亡的日本领导人安倍晋三的巨幅画像前， 鞠躬 致敬。 It had been four years since Mr. Abe, a giant in Japanese politics and the country’s longest-serving prime minister, was shot and killed while giving a speech outside a train station. Ms. Takaichi, his protégé, had come to pay her respects — and to vow to carry on his vision. She told the crowd of right-wing politicians, activists, journalists and business leaders that she sometimes still imagined him sitting on the couch of the prime minister’s office. 安倍晋三是 日本政坛巨头 ，也是该国在任时间最长的首相。他在车站外发表演讲时遇刺身亡，至今已过去四年。作为他的门生，高市早苗前来致哀，誓言继承他的遗志。她告诉在场的右翼政治人士、活动人士、记者和商界领袖，她有时仍会想象他坐在首相办公室的沙发上。 “I could never fill Prime Minister Abe’s shoes; my days are filled with nothing but criticism when compared to him,” she said. “Even so, I want to be a fighter politician like him. I tell myself that I must be.” “我永远无法取代安倍首相；与他相比，我的每一天都充斥着批评，”她说。“即便如此，我也想成为像他一样不停奋战的政治家。我告诉自己，我必须做到。” 2014年，高市早苗（中）与安倍晋三在东京合影。 Since winning election nine months ago, Ms. Takaichi, Japan’s first female prime minister , has frequently leveraged her ties to Mr. Abe to rally support for her nationalist agenda, often referring to him and his policies in major speeches. 自九个月前 赢得选举 以来，日本 首位女首相 高市早苗频繁利用她与安倍的关系来为她的民族主义议程争取支持，并经常在重要演讲中提及他以及他的政策。 She has hailed his vision of a more muscular Japan that is a driving force for strength and stability across Asia. She has invoked his legacy to call for greater military spending and the establishment of Japan’s first intelligence agency since World War II . She has dropped his name while wooing foreign leaders such as President Trump and Prime Minister Narendra Modi of India . 她赞扬安倍晋三关于建立一个更强大的日本并使之成为整个 亚洲力量与稳定驱动力 的愿景。她援引他的政治遗产，呼吁增加军事开支，并建立日本自 二战以来的首个情报机构 。在 争取 特朗普总统 和 印度总理莫迪 等外国领导人的支持时，她也曾提及他的名字。 Yet Mr. Abe remains a divisive figure in Japan because of his break with decades of postwar pacifism; his support for changing how the country’s World War II-era history is taught in schools; and a rise in economic inequality during his tenure. His killing, by a 41-year-old man who was protesting the ruling Liberal Democratic Party’s ties to the Unification Church, a fringe religious group, prompted a range of reactions. While many people were outraged, some sympathized with the assassin, noting his difficult childhood. Others said that a state funeral for Mr. Abe was a waste of money. (His assassin, Tetsuya Yamagami, was sentenced to life in prison earlier this year.) 然而，安倍晋三在日本仍是一个引发分歧的人物，因为他打破了数十年的战后和平主义；支持改变学校对二战时期历史的教学方式；在他的任期内，经济不平等现象出现加剧。他被一名41岁男子刺杀，该男子以此抗议执政的自民党与边缘宗教团体“统一教会”的关系。这一事件引发了一系列反应。虽然许多人感到愤怒，但也有人理解凶手，同情他艰难的童年。还有人说为安倍晋三举行 国葬 是浪费金钱。（今年早些时候，刺杀他的凶手山上彻也被判处 终身监禁 。） Despite Mr. Abe’s complicated legacy, Ms. Takaichi has emerged as one of his chief defenders, hailing him as a transformative leader who elevated Japan’s stature on the global stage. 尽管安倍晋三留下的政治遗产错综复杂，但高市早苗已成为他的主要捍卫者之一，她称赞安倍晋三是一位具有变革精神的领导人，提升了日本在全球舞台上的地位。 This triumphant account of Mr. Abe’s tenure has been on display recently across Japan, including at a sold-out exhibition by the Shinzo Abe Digital Museum, an organization founded by Mr. Abe’s allies in business and government. The exhibition featured more than 100 objects from his life, including the microphone he was holding when he was shot on July 8, 2022, in the ancient city of Nara, Ms. Takaichi’s hometown. 最近，对安倍任期的这种颂扬式叙述在日本各地展示，其中包括“安倍晋三数字博物馆“举办的一场门票售罄的展览，“安倍晋三数字博物馆“由安倍在商政两界的盟友创办。该展览的展品包括他生前的100多件物品，包括2022年7月8日他在古城奈良遇刺时手里拿着的麦克风，那里也是高市早苗的故乡。 安倍晋三的遗孀安倍昭惠（左）出席了一场展出安倍生前物品的展览。 Kentaro Takahashi for The New York Times 2022年7月安倍晋三遭枪击时手中握着的麦克风。 Mr. Abe’s widow, Akie Abe, said during a visit to the exhibition in Nara on Sunday that her husband’s message “has been entrusted to” Ms. Takaichi. 安倍的遗孀安倍昭惠周日参观在奈良举行的展览时表示，她丈夫的使命“已托付给”高市早苗。 Same Playbook, New Challenges 相同的策略，全新的挑战 Ms. Takaichi, who met Mr. Abe in the 1990s when they were both rising politicians and later served in his cabinet, has sought to portray herself as the inheritor of his legacy, at a time when Japan is facing rising tensions with China, Russia and North Korea. 高市早苗在20世纪90年代结识安倍晋三，当时两人都是冉冉升起的政治新星，她后来还在安倍内阁中任职。在日本与中、俄、朝三国紧张局势不断升级之际，她一直试图将自己塑造成安倍晋三政治遗产的继承人。 “She’s embracing what Abe did and running with it,” said Sheila A. Smith, a senior fellow at the Council on Foreign Relations. “她正在全盘接受安倍晋三的一切，并以此为基础继续前进，”美国外交关系委员会高级研究员希拉·史密斯说。 The question now, analysts say, is whether Ms. Takaichi can adapt Mr. Abe’s vision to new challenges. Among them: 分析人士表示，现在的问题是，高市早苗能否将安倍晋三的愿景进行调整，以适应新的挑战。其中包括： • Beijing is rapidly expanding its military and economic influence in Asia, and has led a monthslong campaign against Ms. Takaichi to punish her for a comment she made in support of Taiwan, which China claims as its territory. • 北京正迅速扩大其在亚洲的军事和经济影响力，并针对高市早苗发起了一场持续数月的攻势，以惩罚她发表的支持台湾的言论。中国声称台湾是其领土。 • Japan’s economic outlook has grown more complicated as the country grapples with inflation for the first time in decades and a stubbornly weak yen. • 随着日本几十年来首次面临通货膨胀，加上日元持续疲软，该国的经济前景变得更加复杂。 • The country’s demographic decline is also accelerating, hurting the economy, causing labor shortages and undermining defense priorities like military recruitment. • 日本的人口衰退也在加速，这拖累了经济，导致了劳动力短缺，并削弱了征兵等国防优先事项。 Mieko Nakabayashi, a political science professor at Waseda University in Tokyo, said Ms. Takaichi was clinging to Mr. Abe’s playbook while ignoring new realities. She pointed to Ms. Takaichi’s support for expansionary fiscal policies, which some analysts say could exacerbate inflation. 东京早稻田大学政治学教授中林美惠子表示，高市早苗一味沿袭安倍晋三的策略，却忽视了新的现实。她指出，高市早苗支持扩张性财政政策，一些分析人士称这可能会加剧通货膨胀。 “Her popularity depends on Mr. Abe’s legacy,” Ms. Nakabayashi said. “Her biggest selling point is that she is trying to realize everything that Mr. Abe wanted to do, at whatever cost.” “她的支持率依赖于安倍的政治遗产，”中林美惠子说。“她最大的卖点在于，无论付出什么代价，她都致力于实现安倍想要做的一切。” 在日本与中俄朝紧张局势不断升级之际，高市早苗一直试图将自己塑造成安倍晋三政治遗产的继承人。 Ms. Takaichi worked for Mr. Abe during his first stint as prime minister in 2006, and during his second term, which began in 2012. She rose to the powerful position of minister for internal affairs and communications. 高市早苗曾在2006年安倍晋三首次担任首相期间以及始于2012年的第二个任期内为他工作。她一路晋升，升任总务大臣这一要职。 During that time she became a fierce defender of his policies, including efforts to revise Japan’s Constitution to unfetter its military, and his economic program, which emphasized cheap cash and government stimulus efforts. 在那期间，她成为安倍晋三政策的坚定捍卫者，包括旨在修改日本宪法以解除军队束缚的努力，以及强调低成本资金和政府刺激措施的经济计划。 “I was deeply drawn not only to his qualities as a politician but also to his character as a human being,” Ms. Takaichi said of her work with Mr. Abe, in a letter on display at the new exhibition. 在此次新展览中展出的一封信中，高市早苗如此描述她与安倍晋三共事的经历：“我不仅深深地被他作为政治人士的品质所吸引，也被他作为一个人的人格魅力所吸引。” Tobias Harris, the founder of the advisory firm Japan Foresight and the author of a book on Mr. Abe, said that it remained to be seen whether Ms. Takaichi had fully grasped the lessons of his tenure. He said it was notable that she identified with Mr. Abe’s fighting spirit, given that Mr. Abe’s success in his second term came in part from tempering those impulses. 咨询公司“日本远见”的创始人、一部有关安倍晋三书籍的作者托比亚斯·哈里斯表示，高市早苗是否充分吸取了安倍晋三任期内的教训目前还有待观察。他说，值得注意的是，她认同安倍晋三的战斗精神，而事实上，安倍晋三在第二任期的成功部分源于他克制了那些冲动。 “We have seen her willingness to bulldoze her opponents over and over again,” Mr. Harris said. “But as Abe learned, there is a cost to pay for that.” “我们一次又一次地看到她不惜碾压对手的意愿，”哈里斯说。“但正如安倍所意识到的那样，这种做法是要付出代价的。” 安倍晋三回顾展入口处的参观者。 The Shinzo Abe Digital Museum raised more than $338,000 from individual donors for the exhibition. On a recent day, visitors left notes on a wall with messages such as “You were our hope!” and “We will carry forward your mission.” A shop sold Abe-themed calendars and playing cards that included scenes of him golfing with President Trump. “安倍晋三数字博物馆”从个人捐助者那里筹集了超过33.8万美元用于此次展览。前不久的一天，参观者在墙上留下了诸如“您曾是我们的希望！”和“我们将继承您的使命”之类的留言。一家商店出售以安倍晋三为主题的日历和扑克牌，其中包括他与特朗普总统打高尔夫球的场景。 The exhibition became a gathering spot for his supporters, drawing nearly 7,000 visitors in Tokyo and Nara, including more than a half dozen of Ms. Takaichi’s cabinet officials. 展览成为安倍晋三支持者的聚集地，在东京和奈良吸引了近7000名参观者，包括超过六名高市内阁官员。 Mr. Abe’s supporters are hopeful about Ms. Takaichi, though they said she would face different challenges than Mr. Abe, including disruptions to the energy supply, foreign wars and political volatility in the United States. 安倍晋三的支持者对高市早苗抱有希望，尽管他们表示，她将面临与安倍晋三不同的挑战，包括能源供应中断、外国战争以及美国的政治动荡。 Fumiyo Kato, 48, who runs a weather data company in Tokyo, cried during a recent visit to the exhibition as she viewed Mr. Abe’s personal artifacts: a childhood notebook, a portrait of his father, a wedding photo. title: 对韩国而言，美沙核协议暴露美国双重标准
description: CHOE SANG-HUN2026年7月24日韩国庆州月城核电站附近的一处海滩，摄于2022年。韩国核电产业规模位居世界前列。 Kim Hong-Ji/Reuters For decades, South Korea was an example of the United States’ unyielding stance on nuclear nonproliferation. 几十年来，韩国一直是美国在核不扩散问题上保持坚定立场的一个典型例子。 In the 1970s, the United States pressured South Korea, a steadfast ally with whom it shared nuclear technology, to give up a clandestine nuclear weapons program. Then, it barred the country from enriching its own reactor fuel. The restriction held firm even after Seoul joined a nonproliferation treaty, accepted rigorous safeguards, and built one of the world’s largest nuclear power industries. Nor did the policy waver as North Korea built a nuclear arsenal on the South’s doorstep. 上世纪70年代，美国曾向韩国施压，要求其放弃秘密核武器计划——尽管韩国是与其共享核技术的坚定盟友。此后，美国又禁止韩国自行浓缩反应堆燃料。即便韩国加入了不扩散核武器条约、接受了严格的保障监督，并建成了规模居世界前列的核电产业，这一限制也未曾松动。即便朝鲜在韩国门口建成了核武库，美国的这一政策也未动摇。 Now, the Trump administration has apparently shattered that standard. By striking a deal that could lead to Saudi Arabia enriching uranium on its own soil, Washington has prompted an inevitable question in Seoul: Why Saudi Arabia, and not us? 如今，特朗普政府似乎打破了这一标准。华盛顿与沙特达成一项可能导致其在境内进行铀浓缩的协议，这在首尔引发了一个不可避免的问题：为什么是沙特，而不是我们？ South Korea has long negotiated with the United States for enrichment rights. While its Foreign Ministry declined to comment directly on the U.S.–Saudi accord, it said on Thursday that it was closely monitoring “trends in U.S. foreign policy on the nuclear energy sector” for potential impacts on its own talks. While the deal raises expectations for progress in South Korea’s negotiations with Washington, it could also seed deep friction in the seven-decade-old alliance if Washington continues to ignore Seoul’s demands. 长期以来，韩国一直与美国就铀浓缩权进行谈判。虽然韩国外交部拒绝就美沙协议直接置评，但周四表示正在密切关注“美国核能领域外交政策趋势”对韩美谈判可能产生的影响。虽然该协议提升了人们对韩美谈判取得进展的预期，但如果华盛顿继续无视首尔的要求，也可能在两国长达70年的同盟关系中埋下深刻分歧的种子。 “It is clear that the Trump administration is willing to make major geopolitical bargains with less emphasis on international norms and institutions,” said Leif-Eric Easley, an international studies professor at Ewha Womans University in Seoul. 首尔梨花女子大学国际研究教授莱夫·埃里克·伊斯利表示：“很明显，特朗普政府愿意进行重大的地缘政治交易，而不太重视国际规范和制度。” On Thursday, President Trump said the agreement is contingent on Saudi Arabia normalizing relations with Israel, putting its immediate future in doubt. 周四，特朗普总统表示，这项协议的前提条件是沙特阿拉伯与以色列实现关系正常化，这使协议的近期前景充满不确定性。 Still, the contrast between Washington’s dealings with Saudi Arabia and South Korea exposes a stark double standard in American nuclear policy. Washington appears to have paved the way for enrichment rights for Saudi Arabia for power plants it has yet to build, while denying them to South Korea, which already operates 26 reactors and plans to build more to meet surging energy demands for the A.I. revolution. It has exempted Saudi Arabia from intrusive inspections by the International Atomic Energy Agency, which South Korea has long submitted to to assure the international community that no technology is diverted to weapons projects. 然而，华盛顿对待沙特和韩国的不同方式暴露出美国核政策中明显的双重标准。华盛顿似乎为沙特尚未建成的核电站铺平了铀浓缩的道路；与此同时，它却拒绝给予韩国同样的权利，后者已在运行26座核反应堆，并计划建设更多核电设施，以满足人工智能革命带来的不断增长的能源需求。美国还豁免沙特接受国际原子能机构的侵入性检查，而韩国长期以来一直接受这类检查，向国际社会证明其核技术不会被转用于核武项目。 去年，沙特阿拉伯王储穆罕默德·本·萨勒曼与特朗普总统在白宫举行会晤。 Many in South Korea find this American concession especially jarring given the geopolitical risks. Crown Prince Mohammed bin Salman of Saudi Arabia has openly warned that his kingdom would build a bomb if Iran did. title: 印度青年抗议：一场莫迪始料未及的政治危机
description: ALEX TRAVELLI2026年7月24日周四，新德里街头，人们从抗议标语前走过。 Saumya Khandelwal for The New York Times Narendra Modi, the powerful and acutely image-conscious prime minister of India, is suddenly facing a political problem he had not anticipated on entering his 13th year in office. 印度总理纳伦德拉·莫迪一向强势且极其在意形象。在执掌权力进入第13个年头之际，他突然面临一个始料未及的政治难题。 Mr. Modi has had his eye trained on economic anxieties for much of the year, which were sharpened by the external effects of the U.S.-Israeli war against Iran. His government had to manage shortages of imported oil and gas, distributing the costs among businesses and ordinary citizens. 今年以来，莫迪大部分时间都在关注经济层面的焦虑情绪，而美国和以色列对伊朗发动的战争所带来的外部影响又进一步加剧了这种焦虑。他的政府不得不应对进口石油和天然气短缺的问题，需要在企业和普通民众之间分摊由此产生的成本。 But it was another sort of economic pressure that has now caught up with him and helped drive thousands of students to protest in the capital: The crumbling and sometimes crooked machinery of India’s underfunded education system, along with a painful lack of jobs for the millions of graduates it produces. 但真正让他陷入困境的是另一种经济压力——也正是这种压力驱使数千名学生走上首都街头抗议：印度资金不足的教育体系本身已经摇摇欲坠、腐败丛生，而这一体系每年培养出的数百万毕业生又面临严峻的就业难问题。 After 25 days of protest, and nearly three days since police used batons and tear gas to disperse protesters, Mr. Modi was still struggling for a meaningful response. On Thursday, he posted on social media that “Nothing is more important than the welfare and future of our youth!” He has promised fast-track tribunals to punish the individuals who spoiled the exam but nothing else. 抗议已持续25天，警察动用警棍和催泪弹驱散示威者也已过去将近三天，莫迪仍在苦苦寻找一个有分量的回应。周四，他在社交媒体上发帖称，“没有什么比我们年轻人的福祉和未来更重要！”他承诺将设立快速审理法庭，惩处泄题丑闻的相关人员，但除此之外没有提出其他措施。 This sounded both late and lame to the protesters who were on the street, infuriating many of them further. The movement’s demands are widening rapidly from their initial complaints focused on over accountability for the scrapping of a college-entrance exam to, among other things, compensation for the protesters injured in clashes on Monday. 这番表态在街头抗议者听来既嫌太迟，又显苍白无力，反而让许多人更加愤慨。这场运动的诉求正在迅速扩大：从最初要求对大学入学考试取消一事追究责任，延伸至为周一冲突中受伤的抗议者提供赔偿等多项诉求。 本周，印度总理莫迪在新德里。他于周四首次就抗议者的诉求公开发表评论。 Sajjad Hussain/Agence France-Presse — Getty Images Many of the protesters are students, and many others have jobs, but they share a sense of desperation and rage about education and employment prospects. Smaller protests have emerged in Mumbai, Bengaluru, Ahmedabad and other cities, raising demands that Mr. Modi will find difficult if not impossible to answer in the short term. 许多抗议者是学生，也有不少是上班族，但他们对教育和就业前景都抱有共同的绝望和愤怒。孟买、班加罗尔、艾哈迈达巴德等城市也出现了规模较小的抗议活动，这些诉求将让莫迪在短期内很难、甚至无法作出回应。 Arsh Gupta, a 20-year-old college student, said “there are a lot of feelings” that brought him to the central protest site on Thursday. The original testing failure “is not a small thing at all,” he said, but he was driven more by other issues, most of all “the feeling that we’re living under a dictatorship.” 20岁的大学生阿尔什·古普塔说，促使他周四来到中央抗议现场的原因是“许许多多的情绪”。最初的考试事故“绝非小事”，他说，但驱使他前来的更多是其他问题，尤其是“我们感觉自己生活在一个独裁政权之下”。 At the forefront of the protests is the Cockroach Janta Party, not an actual political party but a movement that takes its name from an insult made by the chief justice of India’s Supreme Court. It is taking aim at these much longer-term crises. The education system is in disarray, the C.J.P.’s spokesmen said, demanding that corrupt and bungling officials must face accountability. 站在抗议最前沿的是“蟑螂人民党”。这并不是一个真正的政党，而是一场以印度最高法院首席大法官曾使用的一句侮辱性言论命名的社会运动。该运动正在将矛头指向印度长期存在的危机。蟑螂人民党的发言人表示，印度教育体系已陷入混乱，要求腐败无能的官员必须被追责。 India’s economy may be growing at a healthy rate, but it offers the protesters little hope. While the gross rate of unemployment looks low, recorded as between 4 and 7 percent, most workers fall outside the formal sector and never get counted. Young adults, especially those who have earned degrees and want to put them to use, are the most frustrated. Nearly 40 percent are unemployed, according to the State of Working India 2026 report published by Azim Premji University. 印度经济或许仍保持着健康增长速度，但这并没有给这些抗议者带来多少希望。虽然官方统计的失业率看起来并不高，大约在4%到7%之间，但大多数劳动者都处于非正规就业部门，从未被纳入统计。年轻人——尤其是拿到学位、渴望一展所长的大学毕业生——是最沮丧的群体。阿齐姆·普雷姆吉大学发布的《2026年印度就业状况报告》显示，印度年轻人的失业率接近40%。 The protesters’ anger intensified after Monday’s show of force by the police, and appears to have turned against the whole of India’s government. 警方周一采取强硬行动后，抗议者的愤怒进一步升级，矛头似乎已转向整个印度政府。 None of this was on Mr. Modi’s menu for 2026. 这一切都不在莫迪的2026年议程中。 本周早些时候，新德里，安保人员发射催泪瓦斯驱散抗议者。 The Iran war presented a tough series of challenges but also an opportunity to make a fresh break. The C.J.P. took up the test-takers’ cause almost instantly. 大约在同一时期，一场全国医学院入学考试的试题泄露事件曝光，导致数百万学生的考试成绩被取消。蟑螂人民党几乎在第一时间站出来支持这些考生。 The protest’s leadership is, however, dispersed and nonprofessional. The causes of India’s jobs crisis have been brewing for a long time. A great deal of students’ time and their families’ money has been invested in courses that routinely fail to equip them for the workplace. 他们所提出的问题同样无法一夜之间给出答案。印度就业危机的根源已经酝酿积累了很长时间。学生们投入了大量时间，家庭耗费了高昂资金投入，但这些课程往往无法真正帮助他们获得进入职场所需的技能。 Amit Basole, an economist and lead author of the State of Working India report, noted that young graduates in India have always been disproportionately unemployed. But their number has grown terrifically in recent years, along with the debt their families owe for their educations. 《印度就业状况报告》的主要作者、经济学家阿米特·巴索莱指出，印度年轻大学毕业生一直以来的失业比例就明显偏高。但近年来，他们的数量急剧增长，与此同时，他们的家庭为了支付教育费用而背负的债务也不断增长。 “It’s a systematic failure. If the government’s not responsible, then who is?” asked Pranavi Tripathi, a 22-year-old business graduate protesting in Delhi on Thursday. “这是系统性的失败。如果政府不负责，那谁负责？”22岁的商科毕业生普拉纳维·特里帕蒂周四在德里参加抗议时说道。 Alex Travelli是时报驻新德里记者，报道印度和南亚其他地区的商业和经济新闻。 翻译：纽约时报中文网 点击查看本文英文版。

His government had to manage shortages of imported oil and gas, distributing the costs among businesses and ordinary citizens. 今年以来，莫迪大部分时间都在关注经济层面的焦虑情绪，而美国和以色列对伊朗发动的战争所带来的外部影响又进一步加剧了这种焦虑。他的政府不得不应对进口石油和天然气短缺的问题，需要在企业和普通民众之间分摊由此产生的成本。 But it was another sort of economic pressure that has now caught up with him and helped drive thousands of students to protest in the capital: The crumbling and sometimes crooked machinery of India’s underfunded education system, along with a painful lack of jobs for the millions of graduates it produces. 但真正让他陷入困境的是另一种经济压力——也正是这种压力驱使数千名学生走上首都街头抗议：印度资金不足的教育体系本身已经摇摇欲坠、腐败丛生，而这一体系每年培养出的数百万毕业生又面临严峻的就业难问题。 After 25 days of protest, and nearly three days since police used batons and tear gas to disperse protesters, Mr. Modi was still struggling for a meaningful response. It is taking aim at these much longer-term crises. title: 美国将对80多个国家加征10%至12.5%关税
description: ANA SWANSON2026年7月24日周一，来自加拿大安大略省萨尼亚的卡车正在排队，准备经密歇根州休伦港进入美国。特朗普总统本周对加拿大进口商品加征了新关税。 Paul Sancya/Associated Press The Trump administration will impose tariffs of around 10 percent on goods from more than 80 countries on Friday, its latest effort to put in place an expansive protectionist policy that has been repeatedly challenged in court. 特朗普政府将于周五对来自80多个国家的商品加征约10%的关税，这是其落实一项大规模保护主义政策的最新举措，而该政策此前已多次在法院受到挑战。 The tariffs will range from 10 percent to 12.5 percent and take effect at 12:01 a.m. on Friday, replacing a global 10 percent duty set to lapse at the same time. Mr. Trump issued that earlier tariff in February, after the Supreme Court struck down duties he imposed last year. 关税税率将在10%至12.5%之间，于周五凌晨0时01分生效，取代届时到期的全球统一10%关税。特朗普于今年2月宣布了此前的这项关税，在此之前，最高法院推翻了他去年实施的关税。 The move provides fresh evidence of Mr. Trump’s intention to transform global trade, despite numerous court challenges and the protests of U.S. consumers and businesses that have been stuck with higher tax bills. Over the past 17 months, the Trump administration has cycled through trade law after trade law as it tries to build a system to shield the U.S. economy from foreign competition. 此举再次表明，尽管法院多次提出挑战，且美国消费者和企业因税负增加而抗议，特朗普仍有意改变全球贸易格局。过去17个月来，特朗普政府不断尝试各种贸易法，试图构建一套保护美国经济免受外国竞争影响的体系。 The duties will be issued under Section 301 of the Trade Act of 1974, which allows the president to impose tariffs on foreign countries that engage in unreasonable or discriminatory trade practices. The administration has cited the failure of foreign countries to pass or enforce laws banning the importation of goods made by forced labor into their own countries, saying that disadvantages U.S. businesses that do follow such laws. 此次关税将依据1974年《贸易法》第301条征收。该条款允许总统对存在不合理或歧视性贸易做法的外国征收关税。特朗普政府声称：外国未能通过或执行禁止进口使用强迫劳动生产的商品的法律，这使遵守此类法律的美国企业在竞争中处于不利地位。 Canada, which will be subject to a 10 percent tariff under the arrangement, already prohibits importing forced labor goods. The European Union, also at 10 percent, has a ban that is scheduled to take effect in December 2027. But Trump officials say that the governments have not effectively enforced those laws. 根据这一安排，加拿大将被征收10%的关税。事实上，加拿大早已禁止进口强迫劳动产品。欧盟同样适用10%的关税，而其禁止进口强迫劳动产品的法规计划于2027年12月生效。但特朗普政府官员表示，这些政府并没有切实执行这些法律。 The United States has arguably the strongest restrictions on forced labor imports of any country. It has prohibited the importation of goods made with slave labor for nearly a century, though it still allows prison labor under conditions that labor organizations consider coercive. In 2021, the United States passed a law banning imports from a region of China where it had found forced labor to be rampant. 可以说，美国对强迫劳动产品进口的限制是世界上最严格的国家之一。近一个世纪以来，美国一直禁止进口奴隶劳动生产的商品，不过，它仍允许劳工组织认为具有强迫性质的监狱劳动。2021年，美国通过一项法律，禁止进口来自中国一个被认定强迫劳动现象普遍存在地区的产品。 The Trump administration also pushed Canada and Mexico to adopt a prohibition on imports made by forced labor as part of prior trade negotiations, and 10 other countries have committed to bans as part of trade deals negotiated over the past year, a senior administration official said. 一位政府高级官员表示，在此前的贸易谈判中，特朗普政府还推动加拿大和墨西哥采纳禁止进口强迫劳动产品的规定；此外，在过去一年达成的贸易协议中，还有另外10个国家承诺实施类似禁令。 But critics say the United States, too, has shortfalls on its labor protections. And some say that the administration has seized on forced labor as merely the most convenient way to reimpose tariffs struck down by the Supreme Court. 但批评人士指出，美国自身的劳工保护也存在不足。还有人表示，特朗普政府不过是借强迫劳动作为最方便的借口，以重新恢复被最高法院推翻的关税政策。 Peter Harrell, a visiting scholar at Georgetown Law School and a former Biden administration official, said that the small differential in tariffs between Canada and the European Union on one hand and China on the other “just brings home that USTR is using this forced labor investigation as a pretext to impose tariffs that Trump wants to impose for his own economic theories and preferences.” 乔治城大学法学院访问学者、前拜登政府官员彼得·哈雷尔表示，加拿大和欧盟与中国之间的关税差异很小，“这恰恰说明美国贸易代表办公室只是将强迫劳动调查作为借口，征收那些特朗普基于自己的经济理论和政策偏好本来就想征收的关税。” “It’s not really about forced labor,” he added. “这实际上与强迫劳动无关，”他补充道。 While Jamieson Greer, the U.S. trade representative, and other U.S. officials have publicly said they cannot prejudge the outcome of the trade investigations, administration officials have privately reassured multiple foreign governments that their tariff rates will end up being the same as in deals negotiated last year, people familiar with the discussions said. 尽管美国贸易代表贾米森·格里尔及其他美国官员公开表示，他们不能预先判断贸易调查的结果，但据知情人士透露，政府官员私下已向多个外国政府保证，它们最终适用的关税税率将与去年谈判达成的协议一致。 “Trump’s next trade scheme is ordering USTR to reconstruct his illegal global tariffs under the guise of addressing forced labor,” Senator Ron Wyden, Democrat of Oregon, said in a Congressional hearing Wednesday. “If the administration wants to get serious about forced labor, the first step is to look at its own enforcement record.” “特朗普的下一个贸易计划是命令美国贸易代表办公室以解决强迫劳动问题为幌子，重新构建他那些已被裁定违法的全球关税，”俄勒冈州民主党参议员罗恩·怀登在周三的国会听证会上表示。“如果政府真想严肃对待强迫劳动问题，第一步就是审视自身的执法记录。” 美国贸易代表贾米森·格里尔周三在国会山举行的参议院财政委员会听证会上接受质询。 The new tariffs will exempt oil and gas and certain national resources, as well as goods already covered under the United States-Mexico-Canada Agreement, or national security-related tariffs Mr. Trump has imposed on cars, steel and other goods. 新关税将豁免石油、天然气及部分国家资源，以及美墨加协定涵盖的商品或特朗普已对汽车、钢铁等商品征收的国家安全相关关税。 More duties are likely to be on the way in the coming weeks. The administration has proposed another batch of tariffs, also using Section 301, on 15 countries and the European Union to offset what the White House calls unfair practices in their manufacturing sectors. An administration official said Thursday that an investigation was continuing. 未来数周可能还会有更多关税出台。政府已提议依据第301条对15个国家和欧盟再征收一批关税，用于补偿白宫所称这些国家制造业中的“不公平做法”。一名政府官员周四表示，相关调查仍在进行中。 Mr. Trump has long maintained that U.S. tariffs on imports were unfairly low, and he came into office wanting to transform that system. But his efforts have been met with plenty of stops, starts and setbacks, reflecting the fact that a president’s legal authority over tariff policy is in some ways limited. 特朗普长期以来一直认为，美国对进口商品征收的关税过低，因此他上任后便希望彻底改变这一体系。但他的努力屡屡受阻、反复启动又受挫，这也反映出，总统在关税政策上的法律权限在某些方面其实是有限的。 The Constitution gives Congress the power to regulate trade, but legislators have written numerous laws that allow the president to issue tariffs in certain circumstances. But typically, those laws are designed to help the president address unfair trade practices in certain countries or industries, not to replace the U.S. tariff system wholesale. 宪法赋予国会监管贸易的权力，但国会也制定了许多法律，允许总统在特定情形下征收关税。不过，这些法律通常都是为了帮助总统应对某些国家或行业的不公平贸易行为，而不是让总统全面取代美国现行的关税体系。 Mr. Harrell said that Mr. Trump’s use of Section 301 was much broader that the statute intended, and that it likely would be challenged in court. While Section 301 was supposed to be used to create leverage to push a country to address an unfair trade practice, he said, “Trump is reinterpreting the statute to try to impose perpetual tariffs on almost all imports.” 哈雷尔表示，特朗普对第301条的运用远远超出了这项法律原本的立法目的，很可能会再次受到法院挑战。他说，第301条本应被用来向他国施压，迫使其纠正不公平贸易行为，而“特朗普正在重新解读该条款，试图对几乎所有进口商品征收永久性关税”。 “They are showing that on tariffs, they can kind of run faster than the courts will, and they’re going to force the courts to keep playing catch up,” he added. “他们表明，在关税问题上，他们的行动速度可以比法院更快，并迫使法院不断疲于追赶，”他补充道。 The Supreme Court invalidated Mr. Trump’s preferred legal tool in February, when it said his use of an international emergency law to impose tariffs was unlawful and ordered roughly $160 billion in tariff revenue to be refunded. Mr. Trump had used the emergency law to announce his “Liberation Day” tariffs on foreign countries last year, and to penalize Canada, Mexico and China for their real or alleged role in channeling fentanyl to the United States. 今年2月，最高法院否定了特朗普最常使用的法律工具，裁定他依据一项国际紧急经济权力法征收关税属于违法，并下令退还约1600亿美元的关税收入。特朗普此前正是依据这部紧急状态法于去年宣布了针对外国的“解放日”关税，并以加拿大、墨西哥和中国在芬太尼流入美国问题上的真实或所谓责任为由施以惩罚。 After the Supreme Court decision, Mr. Trump turned to Section 122 of the Trade Act of 1974 as a stopgap, a law which had never been used to impose tariffs before. Section 122 allows a president to impose a tariff to address balance of payments issues, but it has a 150-day time limit that is set to expire early Friday. 最高法院作出裁决后，特朗普转而援引1974年《贸易法》第122条作为过渡措施。这项法律此前从未被用于征收关税。第122条允许总统为解决国际收支问题征收关税，但规定最长只能实施150天，而该时限将于本周五凌晨到期。 Mr. Trump’s use of Section 122 has also faced legal challenges. A group of small businesses and a coalition of states each sued the administration, claiming that the government did not satisfy the law’s strict criteria. In May, a majority of judges on a federal trade court agreed, handing down the second major tariff defeat against Mr. Trump. 特朗普援引第122条的做法同样遭遇了法律挑战。一批小企业和多个州的联盟相继对政府提起诉讼，声称政府未能满足该法律的严格适用条件。今年5月，联邦贸易法院多数法官支持了这一立场，这是特朗普第二次在关税问题上遭遇重大挫折。 The administration appealed the decision, and the courts have allowed the government to continue collecting the 10 percent tax on imports as the appeal progresses. 特朗普政府随后提起上诉，而法院允许政府在上诉审理期间继续征收这项10%的进口关税。 The provision that the administration is turning to next, Section 301, is more battle tested. Mr. Trump used it to impose tariffs on China in his first term, and his use of it has survived multiple challenges in court. But it has never before been used in such a sweeping way, to issue tariffs on dozens of countries simultaneously. 政府接下来准备援引的第301条经过了更多的司法检验。特朗普在第一任期内曾援引该条款对中国征收关税，且经受住了多轮法律挑战。但以此条款同时对数十个国家大规模征收关税尚属首次。 The administration also turned to another obscure trade law earlier this week, when Mr. Trump signed orders to impose a 50 percent tariff on billions of dollars of Canadian exports. The law, the Tariff Act of 1930, also known as the Smoot-Hawley Tariff Act, was written by Congress to shield American businesses during the onset of the Great Depression, though many historians believe it actually deepened the crisis. The Section 338 provision of the act that the administration used had never been used to impose tariffs. 本周早些时候，特朗普政府还援引了另一部鲜为人知的贸易法律，当时特朗普签署命令，对价值数十亿美元的加拿大出口产品征收50%的关税。他所依据的是1930年《关税法》，也就是《斯穆特—霍利关税法》。这部法律是国会在大萧条初期制定的，旨在保护美国企业，但许多历史学家认为，它实际上加剧了当时的经济危机。而特朗普政府此次援引的该法第338条此前也从未被用来征收关税。 Testifying in Congress Wednesday, Mr. Greer said that the administration remained intent on imposing tariffs, regardless of the legal approach. 格里尔周三在国会作证时表示，无论采用何种法律依据，政府都将继续征收关税。 “The specific authorities this administration is using have changed, but the trade strategy has not,” Mr. Greer said. “We are committed to continuing to use tariffs and to negotiate deals to support the re-industrialization of our economy, protect American workers and increase their wages and shrink our trade deficit.” “这届政府具体援引的法律依据在变，但贸易战略没有变，”格里尔说。“我们将继续坚定地运用关税，并通过谈判达成协议，以支持我们经济的再工业化，保护美国工人，提高他们的薪资水平，缩减贸易赤字。” Tony Romm对本文有报道贡献。 Ana Swanson报道贸易和国际经济新闻，常驻华盛顿。她从事新闻工作已超过十年。 翻译：杜然 点击查看本文英文版。
content: ANA SWANSON 2026年7月24日 周一，来自加拿大安大略省萨尼亚的卡车正在排队，准备经密歇根州休伦港进入美国。特朗普总统本周对加拿大进口商品加征了新关税。 Paul Sancya/Associated Press The Trump administration will impose tariffs of around 10 percent on goods from more than 80 countries on Friday, its latest effort to put in place an expansive protectionist policy that has been repeatedly challenged in court. 特朗普政府将于周五对来自80多个国家的商品加征约10%的关税，这是其落实一项大规模保护主义政策的最新举措，而该政策此前已多次在法院受到挑战。 The tariffs will range from 10 percent to 12.5 percent and take effect at 12:01 a.m. on Friday, replacing a global 10 percent duty set to lapse at the same time. Mr. Trump issued that earlier tariff in February, after the Supreme Court struck down duties he imposed last year. 关税税率将在10%至12.5%之间，于周五凌晨0时01分生效，取代届时到期的全球统一10%关税。特朗普于今年2月宣布了此前的这项关税，在此之前，最高法院推翻了他去年实施的关税。 The move provides fresh evidence of Mr. Trump’s intention to transform global trade, despite numerous court challenges and the protests of U.S. consumers and businesses that have been stuck with higher tax bills. Over the past 17 months, the Trump administration has cycled through trade law after trade law as it tries to build a system to shield the U.S. economy from foreign competition. 此举再次表明，尽管法院多次提出挑战，且美国消费者和企业因税负增加而抗议，特朗普仍有意改变全球贸易格局。过去17个月来，特朗普政府不断尝试各种贸易法，试图构建一套保护美国经济免受外国竞争影响的体系。 The duties will be issued under Section 301 of the Trade Act of 1974, which allows the president to impose tariffs on foreign countries that engage in unreasonable or discriminatory trade practices. The administration has cited the failure of foreign countries to pass or enforce laws banning the importation of goods made by forced labor into their own countries, saying that disadvantages U.S. businesses that do follow such laws. 此次关税将依据1974年《贸易法》第301条征收。该条款允许总统对存在不合理或歧视性贸易做法的外国征收关税。特朗普政府声称：外国未能通过或执行禁止进口使用强迫劳动生产的商品的法律，这使遵守此类法律的美国企业在竞争中处于不利地位。 Canada, which will be subject to a 10 percent tariff under the arrangement, already prohibits importing forced labor goods. The European Union, also at 10 percent, has a ban that is scheduled to take effect in December 2027. But Trump officials say that the governments have not effectively enforced those laws. 根据这一安排，加拿大将被征收10%的关税。事实上，加拿大早已禁止进口强迫劳动产品。欧盟同样适用10%的关税，而其禁止进口强迫劳动产品的法规计划于2027年12月生效。但特朗普政府官员表示，这些政府并没有切实执行这些法律。 The United States has arguably the strongest restrictions on forced labor imports of any country. It has prohibited the importation of goods made with slave labor for nearly a century, though it still allows prison labor under conditions that labor organizations consider coercive . And some say that the administration has seized on forced labor as merely the most convenient way to reimpose tariffs struck down by the Supreme Court. 但批评人士指出，美国自身的劳工保护也存在不足。还有人表示，特朗普政府不过是借强迫劳动作为最方便的借口，以重新恢复被最高法院推翻的关税政策。 Peter Harrell, a visiting scholar at Georgetown Law School and a former Biden administration official, said that the small differential in tariffs between Canada and the European Union on one hand and China on the other “just brings home that USTR is using this forced labor investigation as a pretext to impose tariffs
